title: Linux Foundation launches OpenGrid for power grid planning
key_facts: The Linux Foundation launched OpenGrid to improve grid planning as data centers drive demand for electricity.
It aims to provide a common data and interoperability layer for commercial and open-source planning tools: open standards, APIs and a Data Hub for validated datasets.
The first application, the OpenGrid Translator, is under development and expected in 2027.
The IEA estimates over 2,500 GW of generation, storage and large-load projects await grid connection worldwide.
Backers: Breakthrough Energy GRIDS, Global Grid Catalyst, Connected Grid Initiative and Google.org; technical partners include Open Energy Transition, Tapestry, TransitionZero and QXT Energy.
Alice Yake of BE-GRIDS, chair of the management committee, says many plans rely on unverifiable data and inaccessible tools.
quote_evidence: The Linux Foundation has launched OpenGrid, an initiative focused on improving power grid planning as data centers drive growing demand for electricity.
The IEA estimates 2,500 GW of projects await grid connection globally.
why_it_matters_hint: Open tools could help utilities plan for data center demand, but the first product is a year away.
